input: nums is a plain list of integers, excluding bool. target is an integer, excluding bool. Let n be its length and B its maximum absolute value, or zero for empty input. The shared domain requires 0 <= n <= 4294967295 and mathematical 2 * B <= 9007199254740991 and abs(target) + 2 * B <= 9007199254740991. The number Q of distinct qualifying quadruples must be <= 4294967295; the input, sorted copy and output must fit both runtimes. Lengths n < 4 return an empty result. Empty input is an explicit authored extension, not a claim that the frozen problem admits it; the admitted minimum length must be checked against the pinned contract. Inputs must fit both runtimes; concurrent mutation is excluded. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: A fresh list of distinct, fresh 4-element lists of int values. Each tuple is nondecreasing, uses distinct input indices with multiplicities available in nums, and has mathematical sum target. Every qualifying value tuple appears exactly once. The outer result is in deterministic lexicographic numeric order; its order is part of this paired declaration even if the problem accepts order-insensitively. No solution or n < 4 yields an empty list.
mutation_aliasing: nums, its order, length and elements remain unchanged. Sorting operates only on a new copy. The outer result and every tuple are separately allocated and do not alias nums, the sorted copy, the mutable prefix or each other. The helper's copy, prefix, recursion and result are local; the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: S = 9007199254740991; 0 <= n <= 4294967295; B is the maximum input absolute value or zero. Mathematical 2 * B <= 9007199254740991 and abs(target) + 2 * B <= 9007199254740991. Every pair sum and JavaScript sort-comparator subtraction lies in [-2 * B, 2 * B], within [-S, S]. There are at most two residual subtractions, so successive residuals have absolute values at most abs(target) + B and abs(target) + 2 * B, both at most 9007199254740991. Comparisons compare these exact bounded values directly and do not subtract pair sums from residuals. Count/index expressions, including count - remaining + 1 in Python, count - remaining in JavaScript, count - 1, index + 1 and pointer updates, stay in [-4, 4294967295], and arity/remaining stay in [2, 4]. No products or accumulated full tuple sums are evaluated. Python integers are exact; these bounds preserve exact equivalence to JavaScript Number arithmetic on the declared domain. The bounds are mathematical preconditions, not floating-point validation checks.
complexity: For n inputs and Q returned quadruples, O(n log(n + 1) + n^3 + Q + 1) time under constant-cost bounded-word arithmetic and indexing, with the usual O(n log(n + 1)) comparison-sort bound for Python sorted. Total auxiliary storage including the returned result is O(n + Q + 1); excluding the result it is O(n + 1), including the sorted copy and sort workspace. The recursion has at most 3 simultaneous search calls and prefix length at most 2. Tuple construction costs O(4) per emitted result, not zero. No claim of output-independent constant space is made.

helpers.name: sorted_k_sum
helpers.contract: Only arity 3 and 4 are admitted. Sorts a new copy, then emits each distinct nondecreasing arity-tuple that sums to target, in lexicographic order, using distinct input indices. The helper requires n <= 4294967295, at most 4294967295 output tuples, 2 * B <= 9007199254740991, and abs(target) + (arity - 2) * B <= 9007199254740991, where B is the largest input absolute value or zero. Nested search keeps prefix as the selected sorted values, start beyond their indices, remaining as the number still needed, and residual as target minus the prefix sum; the prefix sum is a mathematical invariant, not an extra arithmetic calculation. Ascending distinct index choices suppress repeated prefixes. The two-pointer base case discards a low endpoint when its pair sum is too small, or a high endpoint when too large; after a match it advances both and skips equal endpoint values. Hence distinct pairs are emitted in increasing first-value order. No pruning or helper contract for other arities is claimed.
helpers.cost: One outer helper call; the complete 1355-byte UTF-8 definition, through the newline after its return result statement, is byte-identical in 0015.py and 0018.py. This includes the nested search definition, all call sites, comments, sorting call, copy and output construction. It is charged in full in each standalone candidate. Search takes O(n^3 + Q + 1) time for this entry point; copying and sorting costs are included in the stated overall complexity. Separator blank lines are charged in total source bytes.

Shared spelling is not a free library: all helper bytes are charged separately in each candidate. Standard sorting time/workspace is charged in complexity.
